## Function Run Mutants

Each planned mutant written over its file, the test command run under a timeout, the file restored; a green baseline first.

Behaviour: runMutants({root, command, mutants: Plan Mutants' Mutant[], timeoutMs, env}) → Promise of {baseline {exit, timedOut}, results, findings}. Every run is acceptance's runAcceptance(command, root, {env, timeoutMs}) (its env rule: the processor's and secret keys never reach the command). The baseline runs first, on the tree as it is; exit not 0 (a timeout is exit null) → results [], findings [baselineFinding(command, baseline, timeoutMs)] = {kind "mutation", source BASELINE_SOURCE "mutation baseline", path null, expected "the test command passes before any mutant: <command>", got "timed out after <timeoutMs> ms" when timedOut, else "exit <exit>"}, and no mutant runs. Else per mutant in order: snapshot = acceptance's snapshotTargets(root, [path]); the mutant's text written over the path by restoreSnapshot({root, entries [{path, bytes: its UTF-8 bytes}]}); the run; in finally restoreSnapshot(snapshot) (an absent file is absent again). result {path, line, column, rule, killed: exit !== 0 (a timeout kills), exit, timedOut}; a survivor gives survivorFinding(result) = {kind "mutation", source "mutation <path>:<line>", path, expected "a test fails on <rule> at line <line>", got "every test passed"}. DEFAULT_MUTANT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000 (the operator's 120 s rule).

Steps:
- uses: acceptance
- reads: Mutant
- produces: Mutant Run

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a tmpRoot holding src/f.ts = F = "export function f(a: number, b: number): boolean {\n return a === b && a > 0;\n}\n"; mutants = planMutants("src/f.ts", F, 10); command grep -q "a === b" src/f.ts, timeoutMs 5000, env {PATH}; when runMutants; then baseline {0, false}; results [src/f.ts 2 12 "=== → !==" killed exit 1], [2 18 "&& → ||" survived exit 0], [2 23 "> → >=" survived exit 0], timedOut false each; findings the two survivors, "mutation src/f.ts:2" expecting "a test fails on && → || at line 2" and "… > → >= …", got "every test passed"; src/f.ts is F again
2. given the same root and mutants; command echo run >> ran.txt; exit 3; when runMutants; then baseline {3, false}; results []; findings [{mutation, "mutation baseline", null, "the test command passes before any mutant: echo run >> ran.txt; exit 3", "exit 3"}]; ran.txt "run\n" (only the baseline ran); src/f.ts is F
3. given lib/g.ts = F, mutants planMutants("lib/g.ts", F, 10); command if grep -q "a !== b" lib/g.ts; then sleep 5; fi with timeoutMs 400; then command sleep 5 with timeoutMs 300; when runMutants; then results [=== → !== killed, exit null, timedOut true], [&& → || survived], [> → >= survived], two findings "mutation lib/g.ts:2"; lib/g.ts is F; then baseline {null, true}, results [], the finding got "timed out after 300 ms"
4. given command test "$MARK" = m1 && test -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY", env {PATH, MARK m1, OPENAI_API_KEY k}, mutants []; then MARK m2; then command true with one mutant {gen/new.ts, 1, 1, "true → false", "x\n"} on a root without gen/new.ts; when runMutants; then baseline {0, false}, results [], findings []; then baseline {1, false} and the finding got "exit 1"; then one survivor and gen/new.ts absent after the run

Data Mutant: One single-point mutant of a code file.
Schema:
{ path, line, column, rule, text }

Data Mutant Run: What Run Mutants resolves to.
Schema:
{ baseline: { exit: number | null, timedOut: boolean }, results: { path, line, column, rule, killed: boolean, exit: number | null, timedOut: boolean }[], findings: Finding[] }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Parse Command

argv into one Command or a usage error.

Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: --pretty, --judge and --write take no value; --root, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches, --slice-cap-bytes, --spec, --component, --map, --out, --checks, --batch, --issue, --seed-file, --from-scout, --scout, --mutants, --mutant-timeout, --test take the next token whatever it is; any other flag (--x=y too) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag last → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag twice → "flag <t> given twice", but --component repeats, its values in argv order (the first error by argv wins). Other tokens are words, giving the command: none → "no command (commands: deck check, plan, run, submit, collect, primer, scout, review)"; "run"; "plan" ("plan --from-scout" when --from-scout is given); "submit"; "collect"; "primer"; "scout"; "review" with two words after it (<base> <head>); "deck" "check"; a first word report → NotYetError "command report is not available yet"; "deck" add|status|reset|clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; else "unknown command: <words, space-joined>". An extra word → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then in order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>", in argv order (deck check: --root, --pretty, --deck, --slice-cap-bytes; run: --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches; plan: --root, --pretty, --spec, --component, --map, --judge, --out, --checks; review: --root, --pretty, --spec, --map, --scout, --mutants, --mutant-timeout, --test, --write; submit: --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor; collect: --root, --pretty, --batch; primer: --root, --pretty, --write; scout: --root, --pretty, --processor, --issue, --seed-file, --deadline; plan --from-scout: --root, --pretty, --from-scout, --out); review: fewer than two refs → "review needs two refs: <base> <head>", a --scout not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--scout must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')", --mutants then --mutant-timeout not a positive integer, else done {name, root, pretty, base, head, spec, map, scout, mutants (null), mutantTimeoutSeconds (120), test (null), write}; plan --from-scout: a value not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--from-scout must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')", else done {name, root, pretty, fromScout, out: null when not given}; plan without --spec → "missing --spec", else plan is done: the plan Command (components [] and map, out null when not given; ## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.
